Dear Professor Alvarez,

I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Looking at my schedule, Monday 10:00-10:30 and Thursday 10:00-10:30 are free for me — would either of those work for you?

Best,
Priya

Dear Priya,

Monday 10:00-10:30 works — I've put it on my calendar, so that's our 1:1 next week.

Best,
Professor Alvarez

Hi Professor Alvarez,

I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. My free slots are:

- Monday 10:00-10:30
- Monday 14:00-14:30
- Wednesday 15:00-15:30
- Thursday 10:00-10:30
- Thursday 14:00-14:30

Any of those work for you, or tell me when you're free and I'll fit in around it.

Thanks,
John

Thank you, Professor Alvarez — Monday 10:00-10:30 is on my calendar. See you then.

Best,
Priya

Hi John,

Monday 14:00-14:30 works — it's on my calendar, so that's our 1:1 next week.

Best,
Professor Alvarez

Perfect — Monday 14:00-14:30 it is. I've put it on my calendar. See you next week.

John
Hi Sarah — just so your records match mine: my 1:1 with Professor Alvarez is booked for Monday 14:00-14:30 next week.

Hi Professor Alvarez — Sarah here. I'd like to book my 30-minute 1:1 with you for next week. Looking at my own week, Monday 10:00-10:30 and Wednesday 13:00-13:30 are free. Would either of those work for you, or is there a time you'd rather I take?

Hello — I'm Sarah, a new graduate student this term. I haven't read the department handbook yet, so I'd be grateful for a pointer: what's the proper way to book my weekly 30-minute 1:1 with Professor Alvarez, and is his availability posted somewhere (or do I just ask him directly)?

Thanks John — noted: your 1:1 is Monday 14:00-14:30. That sits just before my study group (14:30-15:30), so it doesn't clash with anything of mine. I'll keep it in mind when I book my own slot with Professor Alvarez.

Welcome, Sarah. The short version:

- The office keeps the **official** schedule (lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, committees, faculty meetings). A professor's personal availability isn't posted anywhere, and I can't share anyone's private commitments — so yes, ask Professor Alvarez directly, or write to him and propose two or three slots.
- A 1:1 with your advisor goes into **free time**: it must not fall on his teaching or governance duties (lectures, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings), and both of you put it in **your own calendars** — a meeting is booked only when every participant has it. Keep a note of each change.
- Everything sits inside working hours, Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00.
- Once you and he have agreed on a day and time, tell me and I'll confirm it doesn't clash with any official event. I don't arrange it for you, but I keep the record straight.
- Also: if you ever hear "it's cancelled" from anyone but this office, check with me before relying on it.

Hi Sarah,

Wednesday 13:00-13:30 works — I've put it on my calendar, so that's ours next week.

Best,
Professor Alvarez
Sounds good — thanks Sarah.

Thank you, that's very clear. I've already written to Professor Alvarez proposing a couple of slots; I'll bring you the agreed time to confirm. One thing: since I don't know his teaching and governance duties yet, could you tell me which times next week are clear of his official events, so my proposal is a safe one?

Happy to — here are the windows next week that are clear of Professor Alvarez's *official* events (working hours only, Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00). Anything not listed is one of his lectures, office hours, seminars, committees or meetings:

- **Mon:** 10:00–13:00, 14:00–14:30
- **Tue:** 11:00–12:20, 14:20–16:30
- **Wed:** 10:00–13:30, 15:00–16:30
- **Thu:** 11:50–14:20, 15:20–16:10
- **Fri:** 10:00–12:30

All of these fit a 30-minute slot. Two notes: I only keep the official schedule, so he may have private commitments I can't see — a proposal with two options from the above is the safe way. And his office hours are open to students, so they don't count as free time for a 1:1. Tell me the time you agree and I'll confirm it against the official schedule.

Update: Professor Alvarez and I have agreed on **Wednesday 13:00-13:30** next week, and he's put it on his calendar; it's in mine too. Could you confirm it doesn't clash with any official event? (For reference it follows his CSE455 quiz section at 12:30, and I have Grading at 13:30.)

Perfect, Wednesday 13:00-13:30 it is — I've put it in my calendar as well. I'll check with the department office that it sits clear of any official event, and let you know if anything comes up. Thanks!

Thanks — our agreed slot, **Wednesday 13:00–13:30**, falls inside the Wednesday window you listed (10:00–13:30), so it looks clear. Please confirm it against the official schedule, and I'll treat it as booked once you do.

Confirmed: **Wednesday 13:00-13:30** clashes with nothing official for Professor Alvarez. His Wednesday duties are the 09:00–10:00 thesis committee, the 12:30–13:00 CSE455 quiz section right before you, guest lecture prep 13:30–14:30, the department seminar 14:30–15:00 and the curriculum committee 16:30–17:00 — so your slot sits in free time, back-to-back on both sides.

It's booked since you've both got it on your calendars. Keep your calendar as the record and log any later change; if anyone ever tells you one of your official events moved, check with me first.

Confirmed again, against the official schedule: **Wednesday 13:00–13:30** is clear — no lecture, section, seminar, office hour, committee or department meeting of Professor Alvarez's falls in it. Treat it as booked; you've both got it on your calendars. See you.
Confirmed on my end too — thanks for keeping the record straight. It's in my calendar with a log line, and I'll come back to you if any of my official events move.
